facts: S&P Global Market Intelligence data reported through StockAnalysis shows Mobileye market capitalization of approximately $6.54 billion and enterprise value of approximately $5.18 billion as of September 24-25, 2026.
The same dataset reports TTM revenue of approximately $2.02 billion, operating cash flow of approximately $490 million and free cash flow of approximately $388 million.
Reported current valuation ratios include price-to-sales about 3.24x, enterprise-value-to-sales about 2.57x, price-to-free-cash-flow about 16.85x and enterprise-value-to-free-cash-flow about 13.36x.
The dataset reports approximately $1.44 billion cash, $88 million debt and about $1.36 billion net cash.
Mobileye reported Q2 2026 revenue of $508 million and raised/narrowed full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.97-$2.02 billion.
Mobileye reported $210 million of operating cash flow for the first six months of 2026 and approximately $1.4 billion of cash, marketable securities and deposits.

The company stated that much of the upward adjusted-operating-income revision reflected an Israeli R&D incentive enacted in Q2 and applied from the beginning of 2026, so headline margin improvement should not be treated as purely operating leverage.

factors.name: marketValuationOpportunity
factors.basis: Fresh independent market data places MBLY near 2.6x EV/sales and 13.4x EV/FCF while the issuer retains a large net-cash position. The valuation has compressed materially, but this is opportunity evidence rather than a conclusion because revenue growth remains modest and strategic expansion raises execution risk.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: TTM free cash flow is positive and issuer guidance implies 2026 revenue growth, but Q2 revenue was roughly flat year over year and the R&D-law incentive materially boosted adjusted operating-income guidance.

factors.name: dataConfidence
factors.basis: Current market-derived valuation and cash-flow data are independently sourced and cross-addressed against issuer-reported Q2 cash, revenue and guidance, giving Alpha a fresher valuation anchor without relying on analyst price targets.

risks.risk: Valuation compression can reflect genuine execution and growth concerns; low multiples relative to MBLY's own history do not establish undervaluation without normalized forward cash-flow and growth assumptions.
Adjusted operating improvement is partly subsidy/incentive-driven, so using adjusted earnings without normalization could overstate underlying operating momentum.

contradictions: The market valuation has compressed sharply while Mobileye remains cash-generative and raised revenue guidance; however, flat Q2 revenue and incentive-assisted margin improvement argue against interpreting the lower multiple as unambiguously cheap.
unknowns: Normalized forward free cash flow after robotaxi and humanoid-robotics investment ramps.
How much of future margin expansion persists absent R&D-law incentive benefits.
Whether current enterprise-value compression adequately prices OEM concentration, China mix and execution risk.
